precepts.text: A reproof entereth more into a wise man than an hundred stripes into a fool. A foolish person cannot allow wisdom to enter in; you sit around the men, you are in the school with all these men, you see everybody growing around you, but the wisdom cannot take hold because you are fighting against it.
precepts.point: That is why some have been here 10 or 15 years and are still a soldier or an officer of 10. You cannot say you have been held back: you know everything else, but the wisdom cannot take hold and exalt you like it exalts the rest that take hold of it. That is when it is time to take stock in yourself, and a lot of people do not want to do that.

note.label: Character & Integrity: The Hidden Strength Behind Wisdom

precepts.why:
“He that refuseth instruction despiseth his own soul”. He doesn't want to hear it; he doesn't want to be corrected; he's always right, but wrong as hell. That isn't hurting somebody else; you are destroying your own soul, because you can't be corrected, which means you can't grow. This is why: “A reproof entereth more into a wise man than an hundred stripes into a fool.”

As a foolish person, you cannot allow wisdom to enter in. You're sitting around the men, you're in the school with all these men, you see everybody growing around you, and for some reason you know everything, but the wisdom can't take hold and exalt you the way it exalts all the rest who take hold of it. You're fighting against it.

That is why some have been in the truth 10 or 15 years and are still a soldier. How long you been with us? 10 years. What's your rank? Officer of 10, sir. Why? I don't know, sir. You know. You know everything else but that. You can't say you've been held back. Ten years and you're only able to deal with ten men: that is a problem.

That is when it is time to take stock in yourself, and a lot of people don't want to do that, because they don't want the integrity that comes with the Bible. The one who hears reproof gets understanding; the fool takes a hundred stripes and learns nothing.

precepts.text: Children's children are the crown of old men. So it says children's children, grandchildren are the crown, and great-grandkids are the crown of old men. They want to see you have children and keep procreating. They see, like, dang, you came from me, now you are creating life again. Man, I would love to see that thing. Parents love seeing that. And the glory of children are their fathers. So if your father is in dishonour, that means you are in dishonour too. So there is no glory in that. That is why we have got to let our light shine.
precepts.point: For the glory of a man is from the honour of his father. For the glory of a man is from the honour of his father. And a mother in dishonour is a reproach to the children. And a mother in dishonour is a reproach to the children.

note.label: Honor Thy Father & Thy Mother

precepts.why:
“Glory not in the dishonour of thy father; for thy father’s dishonour is no glory unto thee.” Oh, my dad, yeah man, he is broke, he is a bum now, my mom left him behind. That is no glory to you. You came from him. “For the glory of a man is from the honour of his father.” Solomon says the same: “Children’s children are the crown of old men; and the glory of children are their fathers.”

Children's children, the grandchildren, and the great-grandkids are the crown of old men. They want to see you have children and keep procreating. They see it and say, dang, you came from me, and now you are creating life again. Man, I would love to see that. Parents love seeing that.

And the glory of children are their fathers. So if your father is in dishonour, you are in dishonour too. There is no glory in that, and “a mother in dishonour is a reproach to the children.” The honour of the parents and the honour of the children are tied together, one generation to the next.

That is why we have got to let our light shine: so our fathers are honoured in us, and we become a crown to them.

precepts.text: An evil man seeketh only rebellion, which is what Saul did in chapter 15, therefore a cruel messenger shall be sent against him; a cruel spirit sent to trouble him is what we see on Saul.
precepts.point: Chapter 15 said rebellion is as the sin of witchcraft, and Saul is now headed down that downward spiral; the spirit is leaving him, and he will eventually become a reprobate and dabble in real witchcraft.

note.label: 1 Samuel 16: The Lord Looketh on the Heart

precepts.why: “An evil man seeketh only rebellion: therefore a cruel messenger shall be sent against him.” Rebellion is what Saul sought in chapter 15, and now the cruel messenger is sent: “an evil spirit from the Lord troubled him.” A cruel spirit sent to trouble him is what we see on Saul.

precepts.text: Think it not strange concerning the fiery trial; rejoice as partakers of Christ's suffering.
precepts.point: Just as grandchildren crown the old, we glorify our Father in heaven and our forefathers by our repentance and return to righteousness.

note.label: Proverbs 17: Trials That Refine and the Weight of Words

precepts.why:
“The fining pot is for silver, and the furnace for gold: but the Lord trieth the hearts.” The fining pot and the furnace remove impurities from silver and gold; likewise the Most High tries our hearts through trials to rid us of our impurities.

“Beloved, think it not strange concerning the fiery trial which is to try you, as though some strange thing happened unto you.” The fiery trial is not a strange thing; it is the furnace, and we rejoice as partakers of Christ’s suffering.

We must go through trials and tribulations to gain the kingdom. This is why Christianity is false when it teaches you only have to accept Jesus in your heart to be saved forever. That is not what the scriptures say.

precepts.text: Set thy heart aright and constantly endure the trials that will come.
precepts.point: Just as grandchildren crown the old, we glorify our Father in heaven and our forefathers by our repentance and return to righteousness.

note.label: Proverbs 17: Trials That Refine and the Weight of Words

precepts.why:
“My son, if thou come to serve the Lord, prepare thy soul for temptation.” The Lord trieth the hearts, so the one who comes to serve him must prepare his soul for it: set thy heart aright and constantly endure the trials that will come.

That is the furnace of Proverbs 17. We must go through trials and tribulations to gain the kingdom, not merely accept Jesus in the heart and be saved forever, as Christianity falsely teaches.

precepts.text: We must be proven through trials to gain the kingdom.
precepts.point: Just as grandchildren crown the old, we glorify our Father in heaven and our forefathers by our repentance and return to righteousness.

note.label: Proverbs 17: Trials That Refine and the Weight of Words

precepts.why:
“For gold is tried in the fire, and acceptable men in the furnace of adversity.” That is the furnace for gold of Proverbs 17 applied to us: as gold is tried in the fire, acceptable men are tried in the furnace of adversity.

The Most High tries our hearts through trials to rid us of our impurities. We must be proven through trials to gain the kingdom.

precepts.text: We must not glory in a father's dishonor.
precepts.point: Just as grandchildren crown the old, we glorify our Father in heaven and our forefathers by our repentance and return to righteousness.

note.label: Proverbs 17: Trials That Refine and the Weight of Words

precepts.why:
“Children’s children are the crown of old men; and the glory of children are their fathers.” Many of us grew up in fatherless homes, but “Glory not in the dishonour of thy father; for thy father’s dishonour is no glory unto thee.”

We must not glory in a father’s dishonor. Sisters should not speak evil of the man they chose to lie down with and bring in seed by, no matter how bad he is; children raised to despise their fathers must repent of it in this truth.

Just as grandchildren crown the old, we glorify our Father in heaven and our forefathers by our repentance and return to righteousness.

precepts.text: Such a wife is priceless, a shamefaced and faithful woman.
precepts.point: He that covers a transgression seeks love, but he that repeats a matter separates very friends. Covering sin like Ananias and Sapphira, who conspired to lie to the apostles, is condemned.

note.label: Proverbs 17: Trials That Refine and the Weight of Words

precepts.why:
“A gift is as a precious stone in the eyes of him that hath it: whithersoever it turneth, it prospereth.” A well-instructed wife is one of these gifts: “A silent and loving woman is a gift of the Lord; and there is nothing so much worth as a mind well instructed.”

A silent and loving woman does not mean one who never talks. It means a shamefaced sister who is not a chest bumper, a faithful woman whose continent mind cannot be valued. Such a wife is priceless.

precepts.text: Who can find a virtuous woman? Her price is far above rubies and her husband safely trusts in her.
precepts.point: He that covers a transgression seeks love, but he that repeats a matter separates very friends. Covering sin like Ananias and Sapphira, who conspired to lie to the apostles, is condemned.

note.label: Proverbs 17: Trials That Refine and the Weight of Words

precepts.why:
“Who can find a virtuous woman? for her price is far above rubies.” The gift that is as a precious stone to him that has it is the virtuous woman: her price is far above rubies, and her husband safely trusts in her.

She is the silent and loving woman of Ecclesiasticus, a mind well instructed, priceless to the man who has her.

precepts.text: Ananias and Sapphira kept back part of the price and lied to Peter, an example of covering transgression.
precepts.point: He that covers a transgression seeks love, but he that repeats a matter separates very friends. Covering sin like Ananias and Sapphira, who conspired to lie to the apostles, is condemned.

note.label: Proverbs 17: Trials That Refine and the Weight of Words

precepts.why:
“He that covereth a transgression seeketh love; but he that repeateth a matter separateth very friends.” Covering a transgression is condemned. “But a certain man named Ananias, with Sapphira his wife, sold a possession”, and they kept back part of the price and lied to Peter.

Ananias and Sapphira conspired to lie to the apostles. That is covering transgression, and it is the example of what Proverbs 17 condemns.

precepts.text: Trimming thy way to seek love teaches the wicked one thy ways, the ways of the unrepentant.
precepts.point: He that covers a transgression seeks love, but he that repeats a matter separates very friends. Covering sin like Ananias and Sapphira, who conspired to lie to the apostles, is condemned.

note.label: Proverbs 17: Trials That Refine and the Weight of Words

precepts.why:
He that covereth a transgression seeketh love. “Why trimmest thou thy way to seek love? therefore hast thou also taught the wicked ones thy ways.”

Trimming thy way to seek love, covering the transgression instead of repenting of it, teaches the wicked one thy ways: the ways of the unrepentant.

precepts.text: Sin is the transgression of the law.
precepts.point: He that covers a transgression seeks love, but he that repeats a matter separates very friends. Covering sin like Ananias and Sapphira, who conspired to lie to the apostles, is condemned.

note.label: Proverbs 17: Trials That Refine and the Weight of Words

precepts.why:
What is the transgression that he that seeketh love covers? “Whosoever committeth sin transgresseth also the law: for sin is the transgression of the law.”

Sin is the transgression of the law. Covering it, as Ananias and Sapphira did, is covering sin.

precepts.text: Where envying and strife is, there is confusion and every evil work.
precepts.point: Evil begins in the thoughts of the mind, so the strife the fool starts flows from an evil heart.

note.label: Proverbs 17: Trials That Refine and the Weight of Words

precepts.why:
“The beginning of strife is as when one letteth out water: therefore leave off contention, before it be meddled with.” Leave it off before it starts, because “where envying and strife is, there is confusion and every evil work.”

Strife let out is like water let out: once it is meddled with, confusion and every evil work follow. That is why contention is left off at its beginning.

precepts.text: Out of the heart of men proceed evil thoughts, where evil begins.
precepts.point: Evil begins in the thoughts of the mind, so the strife the fool starts flows from an evil heart.

note.label: Proverbs 17: Trials That Refine and the Weight of Words

precepts.why:
“For from within, out of the heart of men, proceed evil thoughts, adulteries, fornications, murders.” Evil begins in the thoughts of the mind, out of the heart.

So the strife the fool starts, the rebellion the evil man seeks, and the evil rewarded for good all flow from an evil heart. Leave off contention before it is meddled with, because what proceeds from that heart is confusion and every evil work.

precepts.text: Thou shalt not wrest judgment, respect persons, nor take a gift, for a gift blinds the wise.
precepts.point: There is no point in a fool holding a price to buy wisdom when he has no heart for it.

note.label: Proverbs 17: Trials That Refine and the Weight of Words

precepts.why:
“He that justifieth the wicked, and he that condemneth the just, even they both are abomination to the Lord.” To justify the wicked is to wrest judgment and take a bribe. “Thou shalt not wrest judgment; thou shalt not respect persons, neither take a gift: for a gift doth blind the eyes of the wise, and pervert the words of the righteous.”

A bribe blinds the eyes of the wise and perverts the words of the righteous, and this perverting of judgment is something we suffer with as a people.

precepts.text: Thou shalt take no gift, for the gift blinds the wise and perverts the words of the righteous.
precepts.point: There is no point in a fool holding a price to buy wisdom when he has no heart for it.

note.label: Proverbs 17: Trials That Refine and the Weight of Words

precepts.why:
“And thou shalt take no gift: for the gift blindeth the wise, and perverteth the words of the righteous.” The law says it twice, in Exodus and again in Deuteronomy: the gift blinds the wise and perverts the words of the righteous.

That is how the wicked come to be justified and the just condemned, the thing that is abomination to the Lord.

precepts.text: Woe unto them that call evil good and good evil, that justify the wicked for reward.
precepts.point: There is no point in a fool holding a price to buy wisdom when he has no heart for it.

note.label: Proverbs 17: Trials That Refine and the Weight of Words

precepts.why:
“Woe unto them that call evil good, and good evil; that put darkness for light, and light for darkness; that put bitter for sweet, and sweet for bitter!” To call evil good is to justify the wicked, and to call good evil is to condemn the just, both an abomination to the Most High.

Those who justify the wicked do it for reward, and the reward usually comes as a financial gift or a place of importance. Woe to them.

precepts.text: The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom; good understanding have all they that do his commandments.
precepts.point: This is why in Ecclesiastes Solomon gives the conclusion of the whole matter: keep the commandments, for that is the whole duty of man.

note.label: Proverbs 17: Trials That Refine and the Weight of Words

precepts.why:
“Wisdom is before him that hath understanding; but the eyes of a fool are in the ends of the earth.” Where does the understanding come from? “The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom: a good understanding have all they that do his commandments: his praise endureth for ever.”

Understanding comes only through keeping the commandments. The fool’s eyes wander to the ends of the earth because he does not have it. This is why in Ecclesiastes Solomon gives the conclusion of the whole matter: keep the commandments, for that is the whole duty of man.

precepts.text: Use few words, especially among great men.
precepts.point: Let thy speech be short, comprehending much in few words; speak only when there is need of thee and hold thy tongue among great men.

note.label: Proverbs 17: Trials That Refine and the Weight of Words

precepts.why:
“He that hath knowledge spareth his words: and a man of understanding is of an excellent spirit. Even a fool, when he holdeth his peace, is counted wise.” Talking too much, especially without the words of the Most High, marks a fool.

“Speak, young man, if there be need of thee: and yet scarcely when thou art twice asked.” Speak only when there is need of thee, and hold thy tongue among great men. Let thy speech be short, comprehending much in few words.

note.label: The Bottle, the Battle, and the Bible

points: The fining pot is for silver, and the furnace for gold: but the Lord trieth the hearts. All those vessels are used for different reasons, but the Lord tries your heart, your mind; he sees what you are really about. Some brothers cannot deal with anything; you do not even deal with yourself, so how are you going to deal with the next man, or with the sisters?
